parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how V. cholerae is transmitted from an infected person to an uninfected person.

V. cholerae releases a toxin called choleragen. Choleragen is a protein molecule made up of six
polypeptides (subunits).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Fig. 3.1 is a ribbon diagram of a molecule of choleragen.
Fig. 3.1
Describe what is shown by the part of the molecule labelled T.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Vaccination can be used to prevent the spread of cholera. The vaccine used contains part of
the choleragen molecule and also contains dead cells of V. cholerae.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Phagocytes play an important role in the immune response to a vaccine. Phagocytes
contain many lysosomes.
Describe the function of lysosomes in phagocytes.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest the advantage of having a vaccine that includes dead cells of V. cholerae and
part of the choleragen molecule.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The World Health Organization states that most cases of cholera can be treated with oral
rehydration therapy. To reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance developing, antibiotics are only
recommended for the most serious cases.
Discuss the consequences of the development of antibiotic resistance in V. cholerae.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Describe the role of the spindle during this stage of mitosis.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The chromosomes are composed of DNA.
Describe the structure of a monomer of a DNA molecule.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Telomeres are located at the ends of each chromosome.
Telomeres progressively shorten each time a healthy human cell divides, until the cell is no
longer able to divide.
Stem cells have an enzyme called telomerase that prevents the telomeres shortening during
the cell cycle.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest why telomerase activity is important in stem cells.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest why tumour cells produce high concentrations of telomerase.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
Scientists have researched the possibility of treating cancer by inhibiting the action of
telomerase.
One method that has been studied involves inserting small, single-stranded DNA into
cancer cells. These sections of DNA have a base sequence that is complementary to a
section of the mRNA transcribed from the gene coding for telomerase.
Explain how inserting small, single-stranded DNA could prevent translation of the mRNA
to produce telomerase.
